merger_name: The State of Western Australia – Mount Lawley Hospital

targets.name: ST JOHN OF GOD HEALTH CARE INC

party_page.name: St John Of God Health Care Inc

merger_description:
The State of Western Australia (the **State**) proposes to acquire the assets of St John of God Mount Lawley Hospital (**Mount Lawley Hospital**) from St John of God Healthcare Inc (**St John of God**) via an asset sale agreement (the **Acquisition**).

Mount Lawley Hospital is a private boutique hospital located in Perth, Western Australia, operated by St John of God. Mount Lawley Hospital offers private healthcare services including acute, rehabilitation and mental health services.

Following completion of the Acquisition, the State will operate Mount Lawley Hospital as a public hospital through Western Australia’s public health system to provide government-funded health services to patients.

events.determination_commission_division: Determination made by Commissioner Williams pursuant to a delegation under section 25(1) of the Act

determination_table_content.details:
The State of Western Australia (the State) applied for a notification
waiver in respect of the Health Ministerial Body’s (a body corporate
established under the Health Services Act 2016 (WA)) proposed
acquisition of the assets of St John of God Mount Lawley Hospital
(Mount Lawley Hospital) from St John of God Healthcare Inc (St
John of God), as described in the transaction documents provided
as part of the application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

After the Acquisition, the State will operate Mount Lawley Hospital
as a public hospital through Western Australia’s public health
system, to provide government-funded health services to patients.
Mount Lawley Hospital is a private hospital located in Mount Lawley,
approximately four kilometres from the Perth CBD. The hospital
currently provides rehabilitation, specialised medical and surgical
services, including orthopaedic, general surgical, urology,
rehabilitation, mental health and allied health services.
Mount Lawley Hospital is currently owned and operated by St John
of God, a not-for-profit Catholic healthcare provider.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. the acquisition involves the conversion of the Mount Lawley
Hospital from a private hospital to a public hospital
b. there are alternative suppliers of hospital services in the
Perth region.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
The ACCC notes that it also considered the potential application of
section 2B of the Act (Application of Act to States and Territories).
The State submitted that making the Acquisition would not involve it
in carrying on a business for these purposes. However, it also
submitted that a waiver would provide regulatory certainty for the
State and St John of God in circumstances where there is some
uncertainty around the application of the acquisition provisions in
the Act to the Acquisition. Having regard to the circumstances,
including the consequences of non-notification, the ACCC
considered it appropriate to make a determination on the basis that
the acquisition provisions in the Act apply to the Acquisition in order
to provide regulatory certainty to St John of God.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
